text:
support-alex: FYI — getting multiple CS tickets reporting 503s from hosted API around 08:15 UTC. Customers see 'upstream inference error' / timeouts. Example req id: req-0a1b2c. Affected customer: acme.ai. Attaching short gateway snippet and runner id.

oncall-mia: I'm oncall, checking now. Can you paste the gateway log lines and the runner pod name?

support-alex: gateway: \"[08:14:58] upstream error: connection reset by peer (runner infer-runner-17-5c9f)\"
runner logs show: \"terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'\" and later \"CUDA error: out of memory trying to allocate 512MB\" then container exit code 139.
Pod: hosted-infer-infer-runner-17-5c9f
Request sample (curl): `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

eng-runtime-jordan: Hmm — SIGSEGV + OOM on the same timeline often points to memory balloon during quantized model path or KV prefetch starving the GPU. Any recent deploys or model swaps?

infra-lee: Autoscaler did attempt to add nodes but pods hit node allocatable limits. Kernel on host: \"NVRM: GPU memory exceeded\" then container restarted. `kubectl get pods` shows many restarts for shard-17. Node pressure on nvmem reported.

support-alex: Customer claims it started after we swapped them to `redwood/quant-2.0` yesterday evening. Their traffic has a lot of tool calls with large context and streaming.

eng-runtime-jordan: Actionable shortlist: 1) pin affected shard to non-quant fallback model, 2) throttle heavy toolcall customers on that shard, 3) capture coredump + gdb backtrace, 4) disable KV prefetch for quant path temporarily. @oncall-mia can you kick 1 now?

oncall-mia: Rolling model pin for shard-17 to `redwood/base-1.3` now, will route new requests to fallback. Also applied a short circuit to limit concurrent toolcall executions per token-key to 4.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback/route-change initiated by oncall-mia for service hosted-infer/shard-17 — start time 2026-03-18T08:22:12Z

customer-success-sam: CS updated acme.ai and let them know mitigation is in progress. Asked them for a minimal repro and sample payloads; they sent a stripped test payload (attached).

support-alex: Repro attempt: send a toolcall with ~80k token context + external toolcall on `stream=true`. After ~25-40s runner memory spikes then OOM and segfault. Repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/quant-2.0","input":"<large-context>","toolcall":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

eng-runtime-jordan: Please capture the core at `/var/crash/core.infer-runner.*` and run `gdb /usr/bin/infer-runner core -batch -ex 'bt full' -ex 'info threads' -ex quit'` and paste output here. Also set `REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0` for quant path in the runtime config to see if prefetch is the trigger.

infra-lee: I pulled a core and ran a quick backtrace — looks like crash inside `kv_prefetch::prefetch_chunk` followed by `pthread_create` related stack. Attaching clipped bt: 
```
#0  0x00007f... in __GI_raise
#1  0x00007f... in __GI_abort
#2  0x0000555... in runtime::kv_prefetch::prefetch_chunk
#3  0x0000555... in runtime::handle_toolcall
#4  0x0000555... in main
```
Host dmesg around the time: `Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (infer-runner) total-vm:xxxxkB, anon-rss:yyyykB` and `NVRM: GPU memory exhausted`.

oncall-mia: Rollback completed. Error rate on shard-17 dropped from ~18% to ~2% in the last 5m. Keeping throttles and model pin in place. Will keep a 30m watch and then lift throttles if stable.

support-alex: :thumbsup: Closing immediate CS escalations and noting mitigation. Leaving repro steps and timeline in the ticket.

eng-runtime-jordan: Follow-ups: create GH issue INFR-2048 with core + clipped bt + dmesg + node alloc metrics. Action items for runtime: a) add guard to limit kv_prefetch concurrency when quantized models are active, b) better OOM graceful degrade to fallback model, c) add a circuit breaker on toolcall path for huge contexts.

infra-lee: We'll also add a temporary node group with higher GPU mem for stress runs and reproduce under controlled cluster.

support-alex: Will attach customer timeline and the small sanitized payload to the GH issue. Thanks everyone.

oncall-mia: Marking incident as mitigated, follow-up required. If error rate creeps >5% I'll reopen the channel.
